name: 2 John

overview.author: “The elder” (1), traditionally identified as John the apostle.
overview.date: About AD 85–95, from Ephesus, around the same time as 1 John.
overview.audience: “The elect lady and her children,” most likely a local church and its members, or possibly a Christian woman and her family.
overview.setting: Traveling false teachers who denied that Jesus came in the flesh relied on Christian hospitality to spread their message.
overview.purpose: To encourage believers to keep walking in truth and love and to warn them not to support false teachers.
overview.structure: Greeting (1–3), walk in truth and love (4–6), beware of deceivers (7–11), and closing (12–13).

items.title: Greeting and the command to love

themes.title: Truth
themes.text: The word “truth” appears five times in the first four verses.

themes.title: Love
themes.text: Love means walking according to God’s commandments.

themes.title: The Incarnation
themes.text: Deceivers deny that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh.

themes.title: Discernment
themes.text: Believers must not share in the work of false teachers.

themes.title: Abiding
themes.text: Whoever abides in the teaching of Christ has both the Father and the Son.

christInBook.text: Grace, mercy, and peace come from God the Father and from Jesus Christ the Father’s Son.
Confessing that Jesus Christ came in the flesh is essential to true faith.
Abiding in Christ’s teaching means having the Father and the Son.

reflection: How do truth and love work together in your relationships?
What does walking in obedience have to do with love (6)?
How can you show hospitality while still guarding against false teaching?
Why does it matter that Jesus came in the flesh?
Who has “walked in the truth” before you in a way that encouraged you?

chapterList.title: Truth and Love
chapterList.summary: The elder writes to the elect lady and her children, whom he loves in truth. He rejoices that some are walking in the truth and reminds them of the command from the beginning: love one another, which means walking in obedience. Many deceivers deny that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. Watch yourselves so you don’t lose what you worked for. Whoever goes beyond Christ’s teaching does not have God. Do not receive or greet such teachers, which would share in their wicked works. He hopes to talk face to face, so their joy may be complete.
questions: How are truth and love connected in this letter (1–3)?
Why should believers not welcome false teachers (10–11)?
What does “face to face” fellowship add to written words (12)?

tagline: Walk in truth and love, and beware of deceivers
readingPlan: 1 chapter: a short book you can read in one sitting, then work through the questions over a few days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
